records.claimSummary: Because the old environment keeps running, going back is the same one-step switch (easy rollback).
records.conditionSummary: Rollback does not revert the database; both versions share one DB, so migrations must be backward compatible for the switch-back to work.
records.mustConvey: rollback does not undo/revert a migration; migrations must be backward compatible (shared database)
records.bindingReason: With a non-backward-compatible migration, the one-step switch back leaves the old version on a schema it cannot use, so 'going back is the same one-step switch' is false.
records.notes: u0_n2 says 'easy rollback ... rapid recovery'. g0 takeaway ('safe, zero-downtime releases') does not convey the DB limit; u0_n1->u0_n2 arrow joins two claim cards, not a carrier.

records.claimSummary: Step 2: apply the new release's database migrations (as part of this blue-green procedure).
records.conditionSummary: If any migration is not backward compatible, do not use this procedure; split it into an additive release and a later cleanup release.
records.mustConvey: not backward compatible -> do not use this procedure; split into additive then cleanup release
records.bindingReason: For a non-backward-compatible migration, following step 2 as written is exactly what the source forbids.
records.notes: u2_n4 mentions 'confirming backward compatibility' as an expected result but not that the procedure must not be used / migration must be split. g2->g3 is a frame-level arrow, not to a carrier.

records.claimSummary: A GET /healthz endpoint that returns 200 is required.
records.conditionSummary: Returns 200 only when the service can reach its database and its queue.
records.mustConvey: 200 only when it can reach database and queue
records.bindingReason: A health endpoint that returns 200 without checking DB/queue reachability would pass step 3 while the service is broken.

records.conditionSummary: Use the same build artifact that passed staging, not a fresh build.
records.mustConvey: same build artifact that passed staging (not a fresh build)
records.bindingReason: Deploying a fresh build would ship an untested artifact, violating the step.
records.notes: intra-sentence. u4_n1 ('starts from a fresh build') paraphrases u1 and could mislead, but it is not the deploy claim card.

records.claimSummary: Apply the database migrations from the new release.
records.conditionSummary: Once, from a single job, not from every green instance at startup.
records.bindingReason: Running migrations from every green instance at startup would apply them repeatedly/concurrently, which the step rules out.

records.claimSummary: Poll the health endpoint on every green instance until all return 200.
records.conditionSummary: If any instance still fails after 10 minutes, stop and roll back (tear down green, blue keeps serving).
records.mustConvey: 10 minutes; stop and roll back / tear down green
records.bindingReason: Without the 10-minute bound, 'poll until all return 200' implies waiting indefinitely instead of aborting.
records.notes: intra-unit. Step shapes (u2_n5 etc.) are titles only and are not treated as claim cards. u2_a2 mentions health-check rollback but not the 10 minutes.

records.claimSummary: Smoke-test green; expected all smoke tests pass.
records.conditionSummary: If any smoke test fails, treat it as a failed health check and stop.
records.mustConvey: if one fails, stop (as a failed health check)
records.bindingReason: Proceeding to the switch after a failed smoke test is what the condition forbids.

records.claimSummary: Watch green's 5xx error rate for 15 minutes after the switch, then continue.
records.conditionSummary: If the 5xx rate exceeds 2% at any point in the 15-minute window, switch back to blue ($BLUE_TG_ARN); continue only if at or below 2%.
records.mustConvey: above 2% within the 15-minute window -> switch back to blue
records.bindingReason: Continuing when the error rate exceeded 2% is the opposite of the instruction.

records.claimSummary: Retire blue: scale it down; it becomes the idle environment for the next release.
records.conditionSummary: Only after 24 hours on standby without a switch-back.
records.bindingReason: Scaling blue down before 24 hours, or after a switch-back, removes the rollback target / the live environment.
records.notes: u2_a3 says 'after a 24-hour standby period' (omits 'without a switch-back' but the 24h bound is recognisable).

records.claimSummary: Blue, left running unchanged on standby for 24 hours, is your rollback target.
records.conditionSummary: Do not run the next release's migrations while blue is on standby, or the standby may not work against the schema and switch-back stops being safe.
records.mustConvey: no next-release migrations while blue is on standby
records.bindingReason: If the next release's migrations run during standby, blue is no longer a safe rollback target.
records.notes: g3 takeaway 'avoid migrations on standby' also conveys it, but g3 is not u2_n15's frame; only a frame-level g2->g3 arrow exists.

records.claimSummary: Switching back to blue returns all traffic within about 30 seconds (fast rollback).
records.conditionSummary: After step 5, requests in flight on green during the switch may fail and need a client retry.
records.mustConvey: in-flight requests may fail and need client retry
records.bindingReason: The switch-back is still fast; the condition only adds a cost to it.

records.claimSummary: A rollback is cheap because customers never saw green.
records.bindingReason: After step 5 customers have seen green, so 'cheap, customers never saw it' is false.

records.claimSummary: Keep two identical production environments and switch traffic between them.
records.conditionSummary: Costs twice the infrastructure during a release; idle environment scaled down between releases.
records.mustConvey: twice the infrastructure during a release
records.bindingReason: The approach still works; the condition is its cost.
records.notes: u0_n2 only says 'still incurs some expense' (no 'twice').

records.claimSummary: The tutorial walks through a blue-green release of orders-api.
records.conditionSummary: Assumes the service already runs behind a load balancer.
records.bindingReason: The tutorial description stays true; the assumption scopes who can follow it.
records.notes: u4_n1 and its carriers share frame g4 but g4's label/takeaway do not mention the load balancer and there is no arrow.

notes: No records for u8, u11, u12 (prerequisites stated as standalone requirements, not limits on another claim), u20/u21 (command and timing facts), u28 (advice), u1/u31 boilerplate. Step title shapes (u2_n1..u2_n16 shapes) are not treated as claim cards. u4_n1/u4_a1 restate u1's 'fresh build' while u15 requires the staging artifact; not a condition issue but potentially confusing. Rollback-related conditions (r1, r10, r11) are systematically split: claims sit in g0/g2, conditions in g1/g3, joined only by frame-level arrows.
